source_text: Demiror itaque ausum te fuisse ponere testimonium, quo dicitur: A quo enim quis devictus est, huic et servus addictus est [n302] . Quod manifestissime pro nobis facit, asserentibus non posse quemquam obnoxium esse diabolo, nisi qui fuerit post certamen voluntatis degeneri deditione superatus. A te autem usurpari non debuit, cui vehementer repugnat, persuadenti in regno diaboli esse nascentes, qui sine voluntate propria nec vinci utique, nec peccare potuerunt.
pass_a_gloss: I therefore wonder that you dared to place a testimony, by which it is said: For by whom anyone has been conquered, to this he has also been bound a slave. Which most manifestly makes for us, asserting that no one can be liable to the devil, unless he who after a contest of will has been overcome by a degenerate surrender. But it ought not to have been usurped by you, to whom it vehemently fights, persuading that those being born are in the kingdom of the devil, who without their own will could at any rate neither be conquered, nor sin.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: I therefore wonder that you dared to quote the testimony: “Whatever has overcome someone has made him its slave” (2 Peter 2:19). This most plainly supports us, who maintain that no one can be subject to the devil except someone who, after a contest of will, has been overcome by a base surrender. You should not have appropriated it, since it strongly opposes your attempt to persuade us that newborn children belong to the devil's kingdom. Without a will of their own, they could neither have been defeated nor have sinned.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
